solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unusual tone about introductions to Gustav Mahler's overture

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters sit around the initials
unusual tells us the letters of tone are set out in an unexpected order
introductions to two names are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A strange tone wraps the opening notes of a Mahler piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Gustav Mahler is only a source of initials here; the overture is Beethoven's, for Goethe's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven wrote incidental music to Goethe's play of this name, best known for its overture.

clue.text: Cryptographer turned red once

indicators.note: turned means turned around or changed, so the letters of red once are rearranged

explanation.surface: A codebreaker once went communist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned red' looks like a political conversion, but 'turned' signals the rearrangement of 'red once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts messages into cipher is a cryptographer at work.

clue.text: Heard Mum speak in French city

indicators.note: heard means what is listened to, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: mum is ma and speak is say, giving ma say

explanation.surface: Someone overhears their mother talking in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: MA SAY, said quickly in a non-rhotic British accent, sounds like the French port's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Mediterranean port is France's second city.

clue.text: You can't leave this way, love, about 11.10 possibly

indicators.note: about means round about, so the letters are moved around
possibly means the letters could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
eleven in Roman numerals is XI, followed by ten

explanation.surface: A sign at ten past eleven tells someone they are stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 11.10 reads as XI (Roman eleven) and TEN; with O for love, 'about' and 'possibly' rearrange the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign meaning there is no way out tells anyone they cannot leave by that route.

clue.text: Poor theologian has no go for operetta

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters of theologian, once go is taken out, are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A struggling theologian lacks drive, or perhaps a turn, in an operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' takes G and O out of THEOLOGIAN to leave THEOLIAN, which 'Poor' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera about a fairy is an example of a light operetta.

clue.text: Aussie parents look up to daughter and son …

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Australian parents look up to their children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LO in a down entry. The ellipsis runs on to the next clue, which is a separate puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang one's parents are informally the oldies, shortened in this way.

clue.text: … looking up to notice on motorway telephone

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
to ring is to telephone

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a sign on the motorway with respect, while phoning.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a motorway running from London to Leeds; its 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To look up to someone is to hold them in high regard, an idiom for respecting.

clue.text: Fashion silver around horse- drawn carriage

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or style

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the symbol is written backwards

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A smart silver-trimmed carriage pulled by a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is Hindi; ton for fashion survives mainly in the phrase 'bon ton'.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled carriage pulled by a horse is used in India under this name.

clue.text: It's all about me. It's me. Go away!

indicators.note: go away tells the letters to move off and rearrange

explanation.surface: A self-obsessed person tells a listener to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go away!' reads as a brush-off, but 'away' signals the rearrangement of 'It's me. Go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive self-regard is the attitude of someone who thinks the world revolves round them.

clue.text: Operatic MOT mechanics

parts.note: mechanics who test vehicles for the British MOT could be called ..., and in an opera theme the phrase points to a Bizet title

explanation.surface: Garage testers somehow turned operatic.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly roadworthiness test for vehicles, so its mechanics are car men; 'Operatic' tells you the title of an opera is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizet's famous opera bears this name, and the phrase split in two describes garage workers.

clue.text: Vow to fellows at old game at the opera

parts.note: I do is the vow made at a wedding
fellows are men
E O, short for even-odd, was an eighteenth-century gambling game like roulette

explanation.surface: A wedding vow made to men at an old game, staged at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: E O (even-odd) was an early form of roulette played in eighteenth-century England.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's opera seria about a king of Crete is a well-known example of an opera.

clue.text: Stylish, frustrating and in a hurry

explanation.surface: A smart person, thwarted and rushing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers being stylishly handsome, crushing hopes, and rushing about.

clue.text: Readies distributed around start of interval included in Verdi's Requiem

indicators.note: around places the rearranged letters on either side of the next piece
distributed means spread about, so these letters are dealt out in a new order
start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Musicians get ready, scattered round, as the interval begins in a Verdi performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges READIES and 'around' puts that round I, the 'start of interval'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin sequence of the Day of Wrath forms a famous movement of Verdi's Requiem mass.

clue.text: Grandma appearing in Queen Bess, Verdi opera

indicators.note: appearing in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: Elizabeth I is Elizabetha Regina the First, written ER I
nan is an informal word for a grandmother

explanation.surface: Granny turns up within the first Elizabeth's court, as in a Verdi opera.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina and I for the First, so Queen Bess is ERI.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's early opera, based on Victor Hugo's play Hernani, carries this title.

clue.text: Jamaican music — short cut to Waldteufel's waltz

parts.note: ska is a Jamaican music style

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: terse means short or curt

explanation.surface: Jamaican music trimmed down into a Waldteufel waltz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the last E of TERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Waldteufel's best-known waltz, Les Patineurs, is known in English by this title.

clue.text: See 20
Those folk admitting piece the same as Elgar's oratorio

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: those folk are them
the king is a chess piece
do is short for ditto, meaning the same

explanation.surface: Some people let in a piece just like Elgar's oratorio.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is the old abbreviation of ditto, the same again.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar composed this oratorio in 1906 as a sequel to The Apostles.

clue.text: One line I found in terrible danger, this becoming a possibility?

definitions.text: One line I found in terrible danger, this becoming a possibility?

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the jumbled word
terrible signals the letters of danger are badly jumbled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A train on one line in grave danger might come off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges DANGER and 'found in' puts I, L and I inside it; the whole clue describes a train at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: A train coming off its track is the possibility the whole clue pictures.

clue.text: Urgent request for parking in front

parts.note: leading means in front

explanation.surface: Someone asks urgently for a parking space at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the standard sign for a car park.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest appeal or entreaty is begging made with passion.

clue.text: Suite by Holst through which thane slept rough

indicators.note: rough means roughly made, so the letters of thane slept are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Scottish lord slept badly through a Holst suite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' is the signal: the letters of 'thane slept' make the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Holst's orchestral suite has seven movements, each named for a world circling the Sun.

clue.text: Highest point reached by plane?

parts.note: the plane is the plane tree, not an aircraft, so its highest point is its crown

explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' wants to be an aircraft; it is the plane tree, whose top is the highest point it reaches.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of a tree, such as a plane, is the highest point it reaches.

clue.text: Date on strange register for Haydn symphony

parts.note: rum is British slang for strange or odd
a roll is a register or list of names

explanation.surface: A date on an odd register for a Haydn symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is old British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Haydn's Symphony No 103 has this nickname from the timpani beating that opens it.

clue.text: Authorisation of meeting with or in Douglas!

parts.note: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man
a date is a meeting or appointment

explanation.surface: Permission for a rendezvous held in Douglas.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, a British crown dependency in the Irish Sea, so being in Douglas puts one on MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An official order or commission granting power to act is a form of authorisation.

clue.text: Prettier elf, not unknown to hesitation

indicators.note: not means the unknown letter is left out

parts.note: an elf is a fairy
Y is an algebraic unknown
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An elf, losing a mystery element, hesitates over who is prettier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes Y, an unknown in algebra, from FAIRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes someone more beautiful, an older sense of fair as lovely.

clue.text: Oratorio by Mendelssohn, I judge, in sound being revolutionary

indicators.note: in puts the I and J inside the turned word
being revolutionary means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: hale means sound or healthy

explanation.surface: A judge describes a revolutionary sound in a Mendelssohn oratorio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being revolutionary' turns HALE into ELAH, and 'in' sets IJ inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendelssohn's oratorio of 1846 tells the story of the Old Testament prophet who went up in a whirlwind.

clue.text: Peaceful girl, alluring one, topless, at end of promenade

indicators.note: topless means losing the first letter

parts.note: a siren is an alluring woman

indicators.note: at end of means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A seductive topless woman at the far end of the seafront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes S from SIREN, and 'at end of' takes the E of promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: This girl's name comes from the Greek word for peace and is borne by the goddess of peace.

clue.text: Oratorio by Haydn in the making?

definitions.meaning: the act of making something, or the universe being brought into being

explanation.definitionFit: The word means the act of bringing something into existence, and is also the title of Haydn's oratorio on the world's making.

clue.text: God making no noise, apparently

parts.note: no is nothing, a zero, the letter O
din is a noise

explanation.surface: A deity who seems to make no racket.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'no din', the name appears to say the god is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief Norse deity, ruler of Asgard, is a god.

clue.text: Respighi's suite is a take on Hitchcock and play by Aristophanes

definitions.meaning: Respighi's 1928 suite based on baroque pieces imitating birdsong
Aristophanes' comedy about a city in the clouds

explanation.surface: A Respighi suite reinterprets a Hitchcock film and a Greek comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The same title is shared by a Respighi suite, a Hitchcock horror film and a comedy by Aristophanes.

clue.text: Timeless blue material as Beethoven symphony

indicators.note: timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: blue means smutty, so blue material is erotica

explanation.surface: Classic smut repackaged as a Beethoven symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' removes T, the abbreviation for time, from EROTICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Third Symphony, first dedicated to Napoleon, is known by this Italian word for heroic.

clue.text: Marie leaves prayer-meeting confused about Grieg's incidental music

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so what remains of prayer-meeting is put in a new order

explanation.surface: Marie walks out of a muddled prayer meeting about Grieg's music.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of MARIE out of PRAYERMEETING to leave PYREETNG, which 'confused' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Grieg wrote incidental music for Ibsen's verse play about a roving Norwegian peasant hero.

clue.text: Couple with a viol from Shetland for Mozart symphony

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair, a couple
a gue is an old Shetland fiddle

explanation.surface: Two players with a Shetland fiddle perform a Mozart symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: The gue is a two-stringed instrument once played in Shetland, islands north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's Symphony No 38 is named after the Czech capital, where it was first performed.
